rounds.text: Savita Oil Technologies Ltd is trading at a compelling valuation with a P/E of 7.97x, which sits well below the sector benchmark of 13.47x [E1, E6]. This discount is completely detached from the company's stellar operating efficiency, highlighted by an exceptional ROCE of 35.34% that vastly outperforms the sector benchmark of 13.91% [E10]. Momentum is explosive as demonstrated by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 37% and profit growth of 323%, accompanied by a rules-based screen score of 87 out of 100 pointing to a clear buy [E16, E19, E60]. The balance sheet is pristine with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and borrowings dropping to just Rs 1 Cr, backed by comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 2.53x [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 943 per share, offering a generous margin of safety of 27.9% [E42, E43]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over 3 years is -13% and promoter holdings have edged down by 2.99 percentage points [E18, E38].

Conceded: [E10]. Beneath the headline valuation multiples, the fundamental earnings performance reveals a persistent structural weakness: compounded profit growth over 5 years sits at -9% and over 3 years at -13% [E17, E18]. This long-term profit decay stands in stark contrast to a price-led advance where share price growth outpaced fundamentals, gaining 22% over 5 years while profits contracted [E21, E53]. Furthermore, the company's return on equity profile is modest at best, with a median ROE over 3 years and the last year stuck at just 8%, well below historical bull markers [E25, E26, E59]. Inside the ownership structure, insider and institutional confidence is quietly eroding as promoter holdings have declined to 68.93% from 71.92%, foreign institutions have trimmed their stakes, and the scanX signal engine flags a negative institutional money flow [E38, E39, E41]. Compounding these concerns, operating margins are explicitly labeled as inconsistent over both the last three years and the last two quarters [E29, E30], while management itself acknowledges vulnerability to significant daily volatility in key feedstock supplies [E78].

Conceded: [E17, E18, E25, E26, E29, E30, E38, E39, E41, E59, E78]. While longer-term profit metrics show past contraction [E17, E18], the business has experienced an explosive acceleration in the trailing twelve months with compounded profit growth surging by 323% and sales compounding at 37% [E16, E19], completely overshadowing historical decay. This operating momentum is fully confirmed by recent results showing quarterly operating margin expanding by 12 percentage points to 17% in September 2026 [E28] and double-digit volume growth across all divisions in Q4 FY26 [E72]. The bear's focus on median ROE figures misses the exceptional current capital efficiency where ROCE reaches 35.34% and ROE hits 25.66%, both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Furthermore, domestic institutional investors have aggressively increased their backing by 5.40 percentage points to 12.80% [E40], overpowering any minor foreign or promoter stake trims [E38, E39]. Finally, management's caution regarding feedstock volatility [E78] is safely buffered by an immaculate balance sheet featuring zero borrowings [E34, E76] and a massive cash and investment pool of approximately Rs 508 crores [E77].

Conceded: [E19, E28, E72]. While the bull points to explosive trailing profit growth [E19] and recent margin expansion [E28], these sharp spikes occur against a backdrop where longer-term compounded profit growth over 5 and 3 years sits deeply negative at -9% and -13% [E17, E18], and yearly operating margins are explicitly flagged as "Inconsistent" [E29]. The bull's highlighted high current ROE [E9] ignores the company's low median return on equity of 8.16% over the last 3 years [E59] and a current reported ROE of 8.3% [E13], proving that the stellar 1-year figures are cyclical aberrations rather than durable capital efficiency. Although domestic institutions increased their holdings [E40], total institutional money flow reads as negative due to promoter trimming to 68.93% and foreign institutional reductions [E38, E39, E41]. Finally, despite a conservative balance sheet [E34], management itself cautions that the business faces significant daily volatility in key feedstock supplies [E78], creating earnings risk that forward-looking statements warn about [E79].

Conceded: [E17, E18, E29, E59]. While longer-term profit metrics show past historical contraction and inconsistent annual margins, focusing on those rearview figures misses the powerful inflection underway, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month profit growth surge of 323% [E19] and quarterly operating margins expanding by 12 percentage points to 17% [E28]. The bear dismisses the sector-leading capital efficiency as an aberration, yet current sector comparisons firmly establish Savita's extraordinary fundamental advantage, featuring an ROE of 25.66% and ROCE of 35.34% against sector benchmarks of 12% and 13.91% respectively [E9, E10]. On institutional flow, the bear ignores the strong vote of confidence from domestic institutions who expanded their holdings by 5.40 percentage points to 12.80% [E40]. Finally, management's cautious stance on feedstock volatility [E78] is easily absorbed by a conservatively financed balance sheet with virtually zero debt [E34] and a rock-solid current ratio of 2.53x [E35].

Conceded: [E19, E28, E40]. While the bull points to a TTM profit surge of 323% [E19] and quarterly margin expansion [E28], these sharp spikes contrast against a history of compressed compounding, with 5-year profit growth at -9% [E17] and 3-year profit growth at -13% [E18], alongside an inconsistent annual margin trend [E29]. The bull's reliance on high ROE and ROCE figures [E9, E10] ignores official filed statements showing a 3-year median ROE of just 8% [E25] and an overall ROE of 8.3% [E13], highlighting a stark divergence in return metrics. Furthermore, domestic institutional accumulation [E40] fails to mask a simultaneous drop in promoter stake from 71.92% to 68.93% [E38] and foreign institutional reduction [E39], culminating in an overall scanX signal engine reading of negative institutional money flow [E41]. Finally, dismissing management's caution regarding significant daily volatility in key feedstock supplies [E78] disregards the company's own explicit warning that forward-looking results remain vulnerable to earnings fluctuations and macro uncertainties [E79].
